title: Chicken or turkey and noodles with tomato-based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of selected chicken or turkey fillet, boiled noodles, and a tomato‑based sauce made from ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic and aromatic herbs. It combines tender poultry protein, carbohydrate‑rich noodles and vitamin‑packed tomatoes for a balanced meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Chicken and turkey are among the most consumed meats worldwide due to their affordability and mild flavor.
The tradition of pairing noodles with tomato sauce dates back to Mediterranean cuisine, where pasta is often served with tomato‑based sauces.
Slow simmering of the sauce brings out the natural sweetness of tomatoes and reduces acidity.
The dish can be easily adapted to dietary needs by swapping regular noodles for whole‑grain or gluten‑free varieties.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes supply vitamin C, vitamin K and potassium, while poultry adds iron and zinc.

items.title: Low in saturated fat (skinless)
items.content: Skinless fillets contain little saturated fat, making the dish suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Noodles deliver quick‑release carbohydrates to sustain energy during active periods.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content in sauce
items.content: Prepared tomato sauces can be high in salt; monitor added sodium.

items.title: Glycemic index of noodles
items.content: Standard white noodles raise blood sugar quickly; whole‑grain options are preferable.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Insufficiently cooked poultry may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot: place noodles on a plate, top with a piece of chicken or turkey, drizzle with tomato sauce, and optionally garnish with fresh herbs or grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat thoroughly to ensure poultry safety.
